knowledge_point.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 16 \\ -13\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 16 \\ -13\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 3 x_{1} \\ - 2 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- 3 x_{2} \\ - 8 x_{2} \\ 6 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ - 3 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 16 \\ -13\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} - 8 x_{2} + 5 x_{3} \\ - 2 x_{1} + 6 x_{2} - 3 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 16 \\ -13\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=6 \\ 3 x_{1} - 8 x_{2} + 5 x_{3} &=16 \\ - 2 x_{1} + 6 x_{2} - 3 x_{3} &=-13\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 16 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & -13\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & 16 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & -13\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & -13\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(2)R_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=6 \\ x_{2} - x_{3} &=-2 \\ x_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(-1)(-1)=-2\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=-3
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-3)(-3)+(2)(-1)=6\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=-1
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=-1$, $x_2=-3$, $x_3=-1$, which means

$$
-1a_1+(-3)a_2+(-1)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(-1)+(-3)+(-1)=-5.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -5 \\ 9\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -5 \\ 9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- x_{2} \\ 0 \\ - x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -5 \\ 9\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} - x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -5 \\ 9\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=0 \\ 5 x_{3} &=-5 \\ 3 x_{1} - x_{2} + x_{3} &=9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 9\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -5\end{array}\right] && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & - \frac{5}{2} & \frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -5\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & - \frac{5}{2} & \frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=0 \\ x_{2} - \frac{5 x_{3}}{2} &=\frac{9}{2} \\ x_{3} &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=-1.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+\left(- \frac{5}{2}\right)(-1)=\frac{9}{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=2
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-1)(2)+(2)(-1)=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=4
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=4$, $x_2=2$, $x_3=-1$, which means

$$
4a_1+(2)a_2+(-1)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(4)+(2)+(-1)=5.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 27 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} - x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 27 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}x_{2} \\ 3 x_{2} \\ x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{3} \\ x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 27 \\ 15\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{2} + 3 x_{3} \\ x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}21 \\ 27 \\ 15\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=21 \\ 3 x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=27 \\ x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3} &=15\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 21 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 27 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 15\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 21 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 27 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 15\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 21 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 27 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -6\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 21 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -6\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 21 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=21 \\ x_{2} + x_{3} &=9 \\ x_{3} &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=3.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(1)(3)=9\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=6
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(1)(6)+(3)(3)=21\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=6
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=6$, $x_2=6$, $x_3=3$, which means

$$
6a_1+(6)a_2+(3)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} - x_{3}=(6)+(6)+(-3)=9.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -11 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}x_{2} \\ - 2 x_{2} \\ 2 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}3 x_{3} \\ - 11 x_{3} \\ x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} \\ - 2 x_{2} - 11 x_{3} \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=4 \\ - 2 x_{2} - 11 x_{3} &=4 \\ x_{1} + 2 x_{2} + x_{3} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & -11 & 4\end{array}\right] && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -15 & 0\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(2)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=\left(- \frac{1}{15}\right)R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} + x_{2} + 3 x_{3} &=4 \\ x_{2} - 2 x_{3} &=-2 \\ x_{3} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=0.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(-2)(0)=-2\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=-2
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(1)(-2)+(3)(0)=4\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=6
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=6$, $x_2=-2$, $x_3=0$, which means

$$
6a_1+(-2)a_2+(0)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(6)+(-2)+(0)=4.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- x_{2} \\ 5 x_{2} \\ 2 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ x_{3} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - x_{2} \\ 5 x_{2} + x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} + 2 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ 30 \\ -8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} &=-11 \\ 5 x_{2} + x_{3} &=30 \\ 3 x_{1} + 2 x_{2} &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 30 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 & -8\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 30 \\ 3 & 2 & 0 & -8\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 30 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 25\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 5 & 1 & 30 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{5} & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -5\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -11 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{1}{5} & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=(-1)R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} &=-11 \\ x_{2} + \frac{x_{3}}{5} &=6 \\ x_{3} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=5.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)(5)=6\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=5
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-1)(5)+(0)(5)=-11\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=-6
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=-6$, $x_2=5$, $x_3=5$, which means

$$
-6a_1+(5)a_2+(5)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(-6)+(5)+(5)=4.
$$
